title: AuthZ & Key Custody PRD — phased acceptance criteria, traceability matrix, and emergency rollback playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Clarify final acceptance criteria for authentication, authorization, and key custody required for Private/VPC customer onboarding. This PRD captures phased gates (alpha -> beta -> GA), the traceability matrix mapping requirements to tests and artifacts, and a documented emergency rollback playbook for keying and auth failures.

Scope: In-scope: SSO (SAML v2.0 + OIDC), RBAC model and enforcement surface for Private deployments, per-tenant audit log forwarding and tamper-evidence, KMS integration patterns (CMEK + HSM-backed KMS), key rotation and custody procedures, and signoff artifacts. Out-of-scope: hosted API multi-tenant identity flows, non-privileged console UX polish (handled in separate DES ticket).

Primary stakeholders: PM (Aisha Patel), Security (Rohit Sharma), Infra Eng (Marcel Nguyen), Runtime Eng (Lina Torres), Legal/Compliance (Marta Ruiz), Customer Success (Daniel Cho).
acceptance_criteria: 1) SSO/SAML: SAML assertions validated by tenant metadata + automated negative test for expired/unsigned assertions. 2) OIDC: ID token validation and session exchange tests. 3) RBAC: role model implemented with attribute-based overrides; automated policy unit tests covering allow/deny paths for all privileged APIs. 4) Audit logs: immutable per-tenant append-only logs exported to customer's destination (S3/GCS/CloudWatch) with SHA-256 checksums and verification tool. 5) KMS/HSM: CMEK key wrap/un-wrap flows validated end-to-end; HSM-backed signing for KMS master key available for customers requiring FIPS-level assurance. 6) Key rotation: documented process + automated rotation test that does not break active KV caches. 7) Tracing & evidence: every acceptance item must link to an artifact (test run, PR, runbook) in the traceability matrix.
scope_changes:
2025-11-24: Reduced initial RBAC scope to platform-level roles + tenant admin (removed custom dynamic roles for GA; to be scoped for post-GA). Rationale: shorten time-to-signal and reduce audit surface for early customers.
2025-11-28: Added emergency rollback playbook requirement after incident review (INC-2025-47) — requirement to be validated in beta.
2025-11-30: Clarified that KMS integration must support both cloud-managed KMS and customer-managed HSM appliances via PKCS#11 gateway (phased; HSM optional for alpha).
rollout_plan:
Phase A (Alpha, internal + 2 pilot customers): basic SSO + tenant RBAC + audit forwarding to S3; KMS via cloud-managed CMEK only. Gate: end-to-end positive/negative tests green, 1-week stability window.
Phase B (Beta): add OIDC, stricter RBAC edge cases, HSM integration tested with one customer. Gate: customer trial signoff + compliance team review.
Phase C (GA): full RBAC schema, multi-region audit replication, documented key custody SLA. Gate: security review passed, legal contract appendix for key custody signed.
Emergency rollback playbook (summary): immediate revocation path for compromised keys (re-key + rotation + KV cache invalidation), customer notification template, rollback runbook link, and postmortem timeline. Detailed steps in links below.
traceability_matrix: Mapping shorthand: AC1..AC7 -> TestIDs -> Artifacts. Example: AC3 (RBAC policy enforcement) -> TEST-RBAC-040 -> GitHub PR #5428, infra-job TEST-RBAC-040 (Jenkins), policy coverage report (drive link). Full CSV attached in artifacts. Each row must include owner, verification step, and evidence URL.
test_plan:
- SSO/SAML: run SAML conformance suite against tenant metadata; negative cases: expired assertion, mismatched audience, replay.
- OIDC: token signature/nonce/time-window tests, session exchange stress tests.
- RBAC: fuzz policy generator to produce 200 role permutations; smoke for privileged APIs and admin console operations.
- Audit logs: verify append-only export, checksum verification tool; simulate log ingestion lag and validate dedup/deferred-forwarding behavior.
- KMS/HSM: key wrap/unwrap roundtrip with live KMS and simulated PKCS#11 HSM; test re-key during active sessions.
- Chaos: simulate partial network partitions and validate graceful degradation and fallback to audit buffer with no data loss.
signoff_checklist:
1) Security (Rohit Sharma) — verification of threat model and pen-test items: artifact link + signed approval.
2) Infrastructure (Marcel Nguyen) — scalability + rollout scripts validated, infra PRs merged.
3) Legal/Compliance (Marta Ruiz) — contract appendix for key custody + export controls OK.
4) Customer Success (Daniel Cho) — pilot customer acceptance and onboarding runbook published.
5) Product (Aisha Patel) — acceptance criteria met and evidence attached.
6) Exec Stakeholder (VP of Product) — go/no-go decision recorded.
Each signer must include date, artifact links, and short rationale in the signoff field of the ticket.

risks:
1) Delayed HSM vendor integration could push full compliance commitments — mitigation: negotiate temporary attestation for GA and schedule HSM for post-GA.
2) Key rotation causing KV cache invalidation and transient errors — mitigation: staged rotation + cache draining strategy and pre-rotation test harness.
3) Audit export downtime causing compliance exposure — mitigation: buffered local store with guaranteed forward-once semantics and alerting.
4) Customer onboarding complexity — mitigation: provide a one-page quickstart and a managed onboarding option for early customers.
